about: Tadaima! compiled dataset — houses and land collected from public portal listings (SUUMO, LIFULL HOME'S, atHome, goo) under the standing brief (<= JPY 50,000,000, <=15 min walk to a station). Facts are as listed by the portals; scores are computed by the open scoring code in shared/app.js. See ../research/ for methodology and ../changes/ for the corrections history.

benchmarks.note: Land benchmarks: average transacted ¥/tsubo by station, 2023–2025, Utinokati (MLIT transaction data). Kawagoe market context: used houses transacted at about ¥96–98万/tsubo in 2025–26; new houses in this city typically ask ¥3,400–4,100万 (goo listing averages). Official land prices rose +1% to +5% across Kawagoe districts in 2026. Tsurugashima (added Oct 2026 for the Shimohiroya section): station-area transactions average about ¥28万/tsubo; Shimohiroya's own plots sit 19–27 minutes out in an urbanisation-control area, which the walk band and the cautions carry.

shimohiroya.note: Added 24 Oct 2026 at a reader's request. Shimohiroya (大字下広谷) is a district on Kawagoe's western edge whose nearest station is Tsurugashima, across the city border — so this section deliberately breaks the edition's 15-minute rule: walks here run 13–33 minutes, and the walk still costs score exactly as it does everywhere else. Much of the district is urbanisation-control area (市街化調整区域), where building and rebuilding need permission; each card's cautions carry that, with score penalties where it bites. The usual ¥5,000万 cap still applies — the one Shimohiroya plot above it (3,931m² at ¥10,000万) is excluded. Same score maths, same benchmarks, nothing hidden.
shimohiroya.noteJa: 2026年10月24日、リクエストを受けて追加したセクションです。下広谷（大字下広谷）は川越市西端の地区で、最寄り駅は市境の向こうの鶴ヶ島駅です。そのためこのセクションでは本編の「徒歩15分以内」ルールをあえて外しています（徒歩13〜33分。徒歩時間は他と同じ計算でスコアに反映されます）。地区の多くは市街化調整区域で、建築・再建築には許可が必要です — 各カードの注意点に、効くところでは減点付きで明示しています。価格上限は通常どおり5,000万円（下広谷で唯一それを超える3,931m²・1億円の土地は収録していません）。スコア計算とベンチマークは本編と同一です。

benchmarks.note: Land benchmarks: average transacted ¥/tsubo by station, MLIT transaction data via Utinokati (multi-year unless noted): Tachikawa ~150 (545 deals; the station average mixes commercial plots, so residential streets sit below it — and a headline '2026 = 308' print rests on exactly one deal and is ignored), Yagawa ~97 (FY2024), Nishi-Tachikawa ~82 (multi-year only: single years swing from 65 to 115 on a handful of deals), Higashi-Nakagami ~79, Tamagawa-Josui ~71 (transactions and official-price estimates agree), Musashi-Sunagawa ~65, Seibu-Tachikawa scored at ~58: the raw transaction average (51) is dragged down by very large fringe lots, while the Ichiban-cho district official average is ~63. Nishi-Kunitachi is scored at ~120, NOT its thin transaction prints (~160 on 2–9 deals a year, station-front skewed): Hagoromo-cho's official residential points average ~107 and the listings here are 7–8 minutes out in low-rise streets. Sunagawa-Nanaban (~85), Shibasaki-Taiikukan (~115), Tappi (~95) and Izumi-Taiikukan (~80) are proxies from official district land-price points (Saiwai-cho ~91, Kashiwa-cho ~96, Sakae-cho ~96; Shibasaki-cho's all-use average of ~226 is commercial-inflated and not used) and neighbouring-station transactions, flagged as such. Walk bands apply Tachikawa's steep observed gradient — prices fall roughly 52% between the station front and a 10-minute walk at Tachikawa station. Used houses transacted at about ¥152万/tsubo city-wide (floor-area basis): Akebono-cho ~184, Kashiwa-cho ~178, Fujimi-cho ~160 at the top; the Sunagawa districts ~119–133. Official residential land prices rose +7.0% in the 2026 survey — five consecutive rises, accelerating (+1.1% in 2022 to +7.0% in 2026).

benchmarks.note: Land benchmarks: residential ¥/tsubo by station, triangulated from MLIT transaction data via Utinokati (multi-year, standardised) and 2026 official residential land-price points via Totinokati/tochidai: Matsudo ~70 (official residential average on 14 points; the all-use station average of ~132 mixes station-front commercial plots — Honcho alone is ~422 — and is not used, and quarterly transaction prints swing from 54 to 115 on 5–7 deals), Shin-Matsudo ~64, Kamihongo ~60 (official points thin at 3, corroborated by its house catchment), Minoridai ~58, Kita-Matsudo ~55, Mabashi ~52, Kita-Kogane ~48 (transaction regression 47.8, official 42.5 and all-use 46.9 converge), Matsudo-Shinden ~46, Goko ~44, Mutsumi/Rokujitsu ~34. Higashi-Matsudo is scored at ~60, NOT Utinokati's ~40 regression: that figure is dragged down by urbanisation-control (調整区域) deals in Kamishiki trading at 3–16万円/坪 on 270–1,000m² lots, which are not residential comparables. Yabashira/Shin-Yahashira (~55) and Koganehara (~43, a district with no station of its own, bus to Kita-Kogane) are proxies from official district points and neighbouring-station transactions, flagged as such. Yakiri (~53) rests on an all-use district print only — low confidence; Motoyama (~44), Akiyama (~57) and Koganejoshi (~56) appear in the house file only and rest on district-level prints, flagged as such. Walk bands use Matsudo's observed land gradient — prices fall roughly 30% by a 10-minute walk and 50% by 16+ minutes (city transactions: 85.4万円/坪 within 5 minutes vs 42.8 at 16+); house prices fall only ~12% over the same range. Used houses transacted at about ¥107万/tsubo city-wide (floor-area basis): Matsudo station catchment ~132, Shin-Matsudo ~123, Kamihongo ~129 at the top; by age, ≤10-yr stock ~139 falls to ~65 for 30+-yr stock. The district print of ~362 for Nemoto rests on a handful of non-standard deals and is ignored. Official residential land prices rose +8.0% in the 2026 公示地価 survey (+8.9% in 基準地価, the Tokyo belt's second-fastest rise) — the fourth straight year of acceleration (+2.3% in 2023 to +8.0% in 2026).

Minami-Osawa (~65), Takao-sanguchi (~30), Mejirodai (~50), Yamada (~52), Naganuma (~50) and the Tama Monorail fringe stations are proxies from official points, flagged as such: Minami-Osawa has no usable vacant-land transaction series at all (prints of 11.3 and 1.1 are developer-era residue). benchmarks.note: Land benchmarks: residential ¥/tsubo by station, adjusted from MLIT transactions via Utinokati and 2026 official points — read the adjustments, because the raw catchment averages describe a car city, not these walkable listings: JR Utsunomiya scored at ~40 for in-zone lots within a short walk (its multi-year catchment average is ~27 because the average transacted lot is a 33-minute walk); the LRT east side: Higashi-Shukugo/Eki-Higashiguchi ~40 (proxy; an official point at Higashi-Shukugo 3-chome prints 54.5), Yoto ~30 (proxy), Hiraishi/Yui-no-Mori-Nishi ~23, Kiyohara/the eastern terminus ~19–23 — the LRT opened in 2023 and its stop-level transaction series is still thin (~70 attributed deals), so every LRT figure is flagged lower-confidence. Tobu-Utsunomiya ~32 (proxy — no station transaction series exists), Tsuruta ~24 (district ~21, standard lots near the station ~26), Nishikawada ~19 (proxy), Suzumenomiya ~18 (official-point proxy), Okamoto ~17, Esoshima ~20 and Minami-Utsunomiya ~22 (proxies by position on the JR Nikko and Utsunomiya lines). Walk bands are nearly flat — land falls only ~9–12% per 10 minutes' walk here — except inside the LRT corridor's developed pockets, where values drop steeply beyond them. Used houses transacted at about ¥69万/tsubo standardised city-wide (floor-area basis; recent transaction averages 73–75): Wakamatsubara ~78 at the top, most established districts 66–78, and age bites hard (a 30-year-old house prices at ~46% of new per tsubo). Official residential land prices rose +1.2% in the 2026 公示地価 survey — the prefecture's all-use figure turned positive for the first time in 34 years — and the LRT corridor's residential point has risen ~3%/yr for five straight years.

benchmarks.note: Land benchmarks: residential ¥/tsubo by station, adjusted from MLIT transactions via Utinokati and 2026 official points: Takasaki ~27 (NOT the 36.2 single-year print and NOT the ~48.7 all-use official average, which is station-front commercial), Minami-Takasaki ~26 (official-points proxy), Takasaki-Tonyamachi ~20, Kita-Takasaki ~18, Kuragano ~16 in-zone, Ino ~15, Shinmachi ~12, Gumma-Yawata ~10 (proxy), Nekoya ~9, the Yamana pair ~9 (proxy), Yoshii ~7 in-zone, Nishi-Yoshii ~6 (proxy), Maniwa ~5. Urbanisation-control land is scored only against control-zone comparables, with its zoning and rebuild status printed on the card — never against these in-zone figures. Walk bands are nearly flat (~−4% by a 10-minute walk on the regression): Takasaki is a car market where the average transacted lot is a 26–34-minute walk, and walk distance is weighted gently on this page for that reason. Used houses transacted at about ¥68万/tsubo city-wide (floor-area basis), flat for five years: the Takasaki station area ~85, Takasaki-Tonyamachi ~78, Ino ~70 (smoothed — not the young-mix 78 print), the central-south ~70, Yoshii ~60, and the western/southern fringe 42–51; 35+-year and pre-1981 stock prices at land value. Sakae-cho's 111 is a 15-case station-front estimate, not a house benchmark. Official residential land prices rose +0.5% in the 2026 公示地価 survey (commercial +1.3%), with centre points up 3–4% and the fringe down 1–2% — a bifurcating market, concentrating on the centre.

benchmarks.note: Land benchmarks: residential ¥/tsubo by station, adjusted from MLIT transactions via Utinokati and 2026 official points: Sagami-Ono ~100 (commercial-mixed at the station front), Higashi-Rinkan ~95 (volatile series), Hashimoto ~90 — adjusted UP, because the raw station figure (~46) is dragged down by urbanisation-control and very large lots; the commercial station frontage is excluded — Sagamihara ~80, Yabe ~80 (thin official series), Fuchinobe ~75 (adjusted up for large-lot drag in the raw figures), Kobuchi ~75, Odakyu-Sagamihara ~70, Sobudai-mae ~60, Aihara ~55 (thin), Minami-Hashimoto ~55 (thin, conflicting sources), Kamimizo ~50 (mixed catchment — Tana-side lots score in the ¥30s), Tamazakai ~50 (thin, indicative), Banda ~42 (thin), Shimomizo ~36 and Harataima ~35 (thin, rural fringe). Sagamiko (~10) and Fujino (~11) are a different, rural market and no listing there is scored against urban figures. Aggregator district prints of ¥200–253万/tsubo in Midori ward and around Sagami-Ono were composition artefacts and are rejected, as is a 2026 year-to-date Midori land print of −20% resting on 5 deals. Walk bands apply the urban corridor's observed gradient — land falls ~20–25% by a 10–15-minute walk on official points; the city-wide band figure (−47%) is fringe-contaminated and is not applied in-corridor. Used houses transacted at about ¥112万/tsubo city-wide (floor-area basis): Minami ward ~125, Chuo ward ~111, Midori ward ~94 on a mixed catchment; by age, ≤10-yr stock ~137 falls to ~73 for 30+-yr stock, which is land-value territory. Official residential land prices rose in all three wards in the 2026 公示地価 survey: Chuo +5.1%, Minami +4.5%, Midori +3.2% — fastest at Hashimoto and Sagami-Ono, flat in the rural west.

Ishikawa-cho is scored at ~116 ONLY for the in-scope southern hilltop streets (Nishitakenomaru/Kashiwaba), from the official point inside that pocket: the prime Yamate-cho points (216–271), the station-front commercial point (299) and the station's residential average (153, which pools points 4 km away in Honmoku) are all rejected for these listings. The Tamagawagakuen-mae listing sits across the Machida border and is scored against that station's Machida benchmark (~62). Kanazawa ward's towns range 49–125 and are scored town by town where they appear. Walk bands use the observed in-zone gradient: 100 / 90 / 78 for ≤5 / ≤10 / ≤15 minutes. Used houses are scored against their WARD, never the city (the city-wide ~156 blends the centre): Kanazawa ~127, Totsuka ~130, Isogo ~132, Asahi ~134, Konan ~135, Seya ~136, Izumi ~136, Tsurumi ~147, Midori ~151 (floor-area ¥/tsubo). Outer-ward residential land rose +2 to +3.5% in the 2026 official surveys — rising, not hot.

benchmarks.note: Land benchmarks: residential ¥/tsubo by station, adjusted from MLIT transactions via Utinokati (multi-year) and 2026 official points (Tochidai/Totinokati): Machida ~95 — NOT the Tochidai station official average of ~181 (commercial-mixed; Haramachida all-use prints 527, the top commercial point 1,028) and NOT the raw ~74 catchment average either (a 20-minute average walk, sprawl-dragged); 95 is the residential ≤15-minute level between the transacted catchment and the central residential official points (116–133). Naruse ~77 (regression 76.8; weighted 2023–2025 ≈78; official 69.4; a 2026 year-to-date print rests on exactly one deal). Suzukakedai ~80 — a deliberate midpoint: the transaction and official series diverge by 25–30 points (101 single-year, composition-skewed, vs 68.6 official) and the gap is unresolved; flagged to revisit first at the next research pass. Tsukushino ~75 (multi-year transactions 68–80; official 71.6–79.4; a 2025 Q1 print of 132 is small-sample noise). Minami-Machida Grandberry Park ~85 (raw ~95 is mechanically inflated by shrinking lot sizes; official 63.9–77.7 lags the redeveloped station front; Tsuruma deals at 79–93 support the premium). Tamagawagakuen-mae ~62 (weighted transactions ≈61.5; a 2026 print rests on one deal). Tsurukawa ~55 (the raw ~51 catchment includes the Onoji/Nozuta urbanisation-control fringe at 27–36; in-zone official residential ≈54–55). Aihara ~40, LOW confidence (2–11 deals a year with ±50% swings; the raw in-zone figure of ~37 is dragged by adjustment-area and 93-tsubo-average lots; the official station average of ~44 is the tell). Walk bands apply the observed gradient: −10% by a 10-minute walk at Tamagawagakuen-mae, −16 to −21% elsewhere — never Tachikawa's steep band. Used houses transacted at about ¥130万/tsubo city-wide (floor-area basis): the centre (Morino/Haramachida/Nakamachi) ~160, the Kanamori belt south ~148, Naruse ~140 (proxy, flagged), Tamagawagakuen ~128, Honmachida ~125, Tsurukawa ~117, the Kanai fringe ~111; age curve ×0.83 at 10 years, ×0.70 at 20, ×0.60 at 30. Official residential land prices rose +3.0% in the 2026 公示地価 survey — rising, centre-led, fringe flat. Data integrity note: these figures were re-verified against Machida's own portal area (city code 13209) during research after an early pass mixed in another city's data and was discarded.

Official residential land prices were flat in 2026 (+0.1% 公示地価), with centre commercial points up 2–4% and the Akagi-foothill fringe down 1–1.5% — a flat, bifurcating market.

benchmarks.note: Land benchmarks: average transacted ¥/tsubo by station, MLIT transaction data via Utinokati (2023–2025 standardised unless noted), triangulated against 2026 official residential points: Mito scored at ~14 in-zone (the standardised transaction average of 11.7 on 420 deals is dragged down by the 382 urbanisation-control deals in the city set transacting at 7.2 and by 60–90-minute car catchments, and the official residential station average of 16.8 on 49 points is the ceiling, not the transaction level — established residential points themselves print 13.3 at Motoyoshida, 16.1 at Kami-Mito and 17.8 at Senba; the all-use / commercial figures are not used at all: Mito station-front commercial official is 33.5 and the top commercial points, Miyamachi at 67.4 and Izumicho at 41.0 in the 2026 基準地価, are a different asset), Akatsuka ~11 (transactions 8.9 on 239 deals; official residential 12.6 on 31 points; near-station points 12.0–14.7), Uchihara scored at ~9 in-zone, NOT its transaction print of 4.9 on 61 deals (its catchment runs to large fringe and control-zone lots; the station-front official point at 5.8 minutes is 10.2 and the Uchihara district transaction averages are 9.6–10.0, while Totinokati's wide-catchment official residential average of 7.6 folds in farm-fringe points — in-zone streets near the station sit at ~9), Higashi-Mito ~8 as a flagged proxy, NOT its transaction print of 1.1 on just 6 deals (a thin, fringe-dragged print that says nothing about the built-up streets 3.8 km from Mito station; no isolated official station average was verified in this pass, so the figure is interpolated between Mito in-zone and Tsunezumi and must be treated as provisional), Tsunezumi ~7 (transactions 6.9 on 10 deals and official residential 7.1 on 3 points agree — thin but consistent). Kairakuen is a temporary, plum-season-only station and is scored as Mito; the Suigun Line has no station in Mito City other than Mito itself. Walk bands apply Mito's exceptionally flat observed gradient — Utinokati's regression puts the fall at only ~0.9% by a 10-minute walk, the average transacted land walk is ~37 minutes and the average transacted house walk ~32 minutes; this is a car-and-bus city and walk minutes must be weighted gently, exactly as in Takasaki and the opposite of Tachikawa. Used houses transacted at about ¥61万/tsubo city-wide (floor-area basis; Utinokati city average information: ¥2,897万 average price, average age 19.5 years, 5,199 deals in the all-period area table). Official residential land prices were flat in 2026 (公示-based station averages: Mito +0.0%, Akatsuka +0.0%, Uchihara −0.1%; 基準地価 city average +0.2 to +0.5% depending on averaging method, with rises confined to station-front commercial points at +1.8 to +2.5% and fringe residential points at −0.8 to −0.9%) — a stable regional capital, not a rising Tokyo suburb. Two Suigun Line stations in Hitachinaka City also serve Mito districts in this collection and are scored as documented exceptions: Hitachi-Aoyagi ~5 as a flagged proxy, NOT its single-deal prints of 1.0 (2025, 1 deal) and 2.0 (2024, 1 deal) or its all-period standardised 3.2 on 25 deals (its walkable catchment — Mito's Aoyagi-cho and Hitachinaka's Edagawa, in the Naka River lowland — is entirely urbanisation-control, every zoning-attributed deal in the station set is control-zoned, and no in-zone figure exists to measure; ~5 is the level for buildable lots in the established anyone-may-build pockets, resting on the 2026 official residential points at Aoyagi-cho 7.7 and Edagawa 4.4 and on current buildable-lot asking prices centred around 5), Hitachi-Tsuda ~6 (the station average-information of 3.6 on 113 deals and the Oaza Tsuda district standardised 3.8 are dragged down by 200-tsubo-plus control and farmland-scale lots printing at 0.0–0.3; residential-sized buildable deals in 2023–2025 cluster at 4.7–8.1 with a median around 5.6, and the 2026 official point in Oaza Tsuda is 6.38; the genuinely in-zone Ichige subdivisions on the Katsuta side, transacting around 12.5, are a different product and are checked individually, never blended into the station figure).

benchmarks.note: Land benchmarks: residential ¥/tsubo by station, triangulated from MLIT transaction data via Utinokati and 2026 official residential land-price points via Totinokati/tochidai: Kasukabe ~48 (residential points at an 8–13-minute walk are 47–51; the all-use station average of ~50 mixes the station-front commercial point at ~122 and the Kasukabe district print of ~83 and is not used as a level, and Utinokati's ~63 regression for the Chuo district is a station-front district figure, not a residential one), Takesato ~33, Ichinowari ~30, Kita-Kasukabe ~26, Fujino-Ushijima ~25, Minami-Sakurai ~19. The city-wide official residential averages (~30 公示 / ~25 基準） are catchment averages whose point sets include farmhouse points a 30–45-minute walk from any station — one prints 6.0万円/坪 at a 42-minute walk — and are not used as station benchmarks. Fujino-Ushijima is scored at ~25 from its two station-front official points (24.6 and 25.0), NOT from any blended transaction average: in that catchment, urbanisation-area lots at a 4-minute walk print 34–43万円/坪 while urbanisation-control （調整区域） plots print 2–10万円/坪, and one quarterly station print of 2.3万円/坪 rests on exactly 2 control-area deals averaging 424 tsubo. Takesato (~33), Ichinowari (~30) and Kita-Kasukabe (~26) are proxies from all-use station averages bracketed by neighbouring official points, flagged as such; Himemiya (~22) is a pure proxy — no official point or published station average could be isolated for it. Sengendai is not benchmarked: it is in Koshigaya, and Kasukabe's Chima-side deals that name it belong to that market. Walk bands use Kasukabe's own observed gradient — the official regression over the city's residential points calls it gentle (elasticity −2.81): land falls roughly 10–15% by an 11–15-minute walk and 25–30% by 16+ minutes, and houses only ~15% over the same range. Used houses transacted at about ¥74万/tsubo city-wide (floor-area basis, recent-3-year average; the Kasukabe station catchment standardises to ~88 on a mean 17-minute walk): by age, ≤10-yr stock ~96 falls to ~58 at 20–30 years and ~39–48 beyond 30 years. Single-year district prints in Kasukabe rest on handfuls of deals (one district's "99" is 3 near-new houses; another's "22" is 2 deals) and are ignored. Official residential land prices were flat in 2026 (+0.1% 公示地価， median point +0.0%; +0.2% 基準地価） — the stillest market in the set, with some station tax-value series unchanged for a decade. A later top-up pass added the two in-city Tobu Urban Park Line stations the first brief missed: Yagisaki ~36 (2026 official points on its side print 33.7–41.0; the raw all-period mean of 30.2 is dragged by 93.6-tsubo average lots, and its 2026 print of 20.3 rests on exactly one deal) and Toyoharu ~32 (full-year MLIT averages of 30.1 in 2024 and 31.7 in 2025; the 2026 print of 50.0 rests on exactly two deals, and Utinokati's 24.4 regression catchment includes control-area deals at 3.9–9.1). Houses at both stations score against the same city anchor (~74) and age cohorts — Yagisakicho standardises to ~73.5 — with no invented station discount.

benchmarks.note: Land benchmarks: residential ¥/tsubo by station, triangulated from MLIT transaction data via Utinokati (multi-year, standardised) and 2026 official residential land-price points via Totinokati/tochidai: Shin-Koshigaya/Minami-Koshigaya ~80 (official residential average 76.3 on 9 points, with core residential points at 73–91 within 5–8 minutes; the all-use station average of ~99 and the commercial-point average of ~156 — station-front plots at 157–180 with 400% floor-area ratio — are not used, because the listings are houses and residential lots on side streets), Koshigaya-Laketown ~65 (residential points 58.5–72.1; district averages of ~70–76 are not used because they include a single 95.5 point on a 391m² plot), Koshigaya ~60 (the official station average of ~52 pools points out to 25 minutes; points at 6–15 minutes run 57–91 and sampled transactions at 16 minutes print 55–59), Gamo ~55, Kita-Koshigaya ~50, Sengendai ~42, Obukuro ~40. Kita-Koshigaya is scored at ~50, NOT the official catchment average of ~39: that average is dragged down by urbanisation-control (調整区域) and farmhouse-fringe points and deals — control-area plots in its catchment trade at 4–26万円/坪 — while the Osawa district transaction regression is ~52 (23 deals) and its 15-minute official point is ~45. Higashi-Koshigaya (~55) and Osawa (~50) are districts, not stations — their nearest stations are Koshigaya and Kita-Koshigaya — and are scored from district official points and transactions, flagged as such. Walk bands use Koshigaya's observed land gradient — official points fall roughly 30% by a 10-minute walk and 45–50% by 16+ minutes (Koshigaya station: ~91 within 6 minutes vs ~41–44 beyond 20 minutes); house prices fall only ~20% over the same range. Used houses transacted at about ¥101万/tsubo city-wide (floor-area basis, regression on 2,150 deals): Akayamacho ~123 and the Koshigaya station districts ~116 at the top; by age (Gamo district series, used as the shape proxy), ≤10-yr stock ~139 falls to ~65 for 30+-yr stock. The Shin-Koshigaya district simple average of ~174 rests on a thin slice of new station-adjacent stock and is ignored as a level. Official residential land prices rose +3.2% in the 2026 公示地価 survey (30 of 32 points up, none down) — the fifth straight year of acceleration (+0.5% in 2022 to +3.5% in 2026) — with station-side points up 5–6% and the adjustment-area fringe flat.

benchmarks.note: Land benchmarks: residential ¥/tsubo by station, triangulated from MLIT transaction data via Utinokati (multi-year) and 2026 official residential land-price points via Totinokati/tochidai: Ichikawa ~125 (official residential points run 132–146 at a 9–15 minute walk and the tax-valuation series implies ~124; the raw station transaction average of ~95 pools 16+ minute fringe deals and is not used, and the district regression of ~137 rests on only 24 analysis deals), Ichikawa-Mama ~130 and Sugano ~130 (proxies from official points — Mama 2-chome and Sugano 3-chome both print ~144 — and Sugano-side district transactions ~125–132), Motoyawata ~110 (137 transactions average ~102 and the official series implies ~109; tochidai's all-use station average of ~306 is station-front commercial — Yawata 2-chome alone is ~919 — and is not used), Keisei-Yawata ~120 and Onigoe ~100 (proxies: Yawata district transactions print ~145 on 19 deals while Onigoe's ~132 rests on just 5 deals against an all-period ~93–97, so both are scored below the thin prints), Shimosa-Nakayama ~95, Baraki-Nakayama ~78, Gyotoku ~125 and Myoden ~120 (their raw transaction averages of ~164 and ~141 are small-lot, station-front-skewed prints on 25 and 17 deals — Gyotoku-Ekimae commercial deals reach ~211 — while the official series implies ~123–126 and Myoden district's own regression is ~105), Minami-Gyotoku ~115, Ichikawa-Ono ~45 (transactions ~42 on 48 deals and official points 44–50 converge), Oomachi ~28 (pear-farming fringe; the district's ¥22.5 基準地価 average includes farm and forest points). Ichikawa-Shiohama (~90) and Futamata-Shinmachi (~45) are flagged very-low-confidence proxies for Keiyo-line stations whose surroundings are industrial-exclusive zoning with no residential market — any listing there actually sits in a neighbouring district and should be scored there. City-wide, urbanisation-control （調整区域） deals average ~37万円/坪 (52 deals) and drag every northern catchment they touch. Walk bands use Ichikawa's observed gradient — land prices fall roughly 33% by a 10-minute walk (city regression) and over 50% by 16+ minutes (transactions: 134.3万円/坪 within 5 minutes vs 58.7 at 16+); house prices fall only ~15% by 10 minutes and ~35% by 16+. Used houses transacted at about ¥139万/tsubo city-wide (floor-area basis, standardised; 2025 simple average ~150): Gyotoku ~167, Myoden ~162, Motoyawata ~158 at the top, Ichikawa-Ono ~105 in the north; by age, ≤10-yr stock ~173 falls to ~95 for 30+-yr stock. The district house prints of ~316 for Futamata (13 deals) and ~233 for Takaya (17 deals) are mix artefacts and are ignored. Official residential land prices rose +3.4% in the 2026 基準地価 survey (station pockets +4–6%) — a steady, broad rise, slightly slower than 2025's +3.9%.

benchmarks.note: Land benchmarks: residential ¥/tsubo by station, triangulated from MLIT transaction data via Utinokati (multi-year, standardised) and 2026 official residential land-price points via Totinokati/tochidai: Fujisawa ~95 (transactions run 97–108 across three lenses and official points at 9–13 minutes run 98–142; the official whole-catchment residential average of ~78 is dragged down by 20+-minute fringe points, and the all-use station average of ~130 mixes station-front commercial plots — Minami-Fujisawa alone is ~704 — and is not used), Tsujido ~95 (official residential 96.3 on 11 points and the transaction regression 95.1 converge), Shonandai ~90 (official residential 90.9 on 14 points; its all-use district average of ~119 is station-front commercial and is not used), Hon-Kugenuma ~95, Kugenuma-Kaigan ~90, Fujisawa-Honmachi ~70 (official points 65.1, transaction regression 79.2), Zengyo ~60, Mutsuai-Nichidai-mae ~58, Chogo ~50. Katase-Enoshima is scored at ~110 as a flagged proxy blend, NOT its annual transaction prints of 133–186, which rest on roughly two deals a year in the Katase-Kaigan shore strip: shore-strip streets score at ~135 and inland Katase streets at ~85, because the coastal premium here is a separate market inside the same station catchment — the same split, smaller, applies in Kugenuma (Sakuragaoka/Matsugaoka and the Kugenuma-Kaigan shore streets run 10–25% above the station figures) and barely at all in Tsujido. The Enoden local stations are scored from multi-year transactions cross-checked against official points: Ishigami ~95 (proxy — Fujisawa station's south side; no residential official point is assigned to it), Yanagikoji ~90, Kugenuma ~85, Shonankaigan-koen ~75, Enoshima ~80 (proxy; no residential official point). Northern averages are scored in-zone only: urbanisation-control deals in Kuzuhara, Endo, Imada and Yoda trade at 2–27万円/坪 (the city's lowest official point is 1.5 in Kuzuhara, and its only falling 2026 residential point is Imada at 15.2) and are never used as residential comparables. Walk bands use Fujisawa's observed gradients — land falls about 35% by a 10-minute walk at Fujisawa station (−21.6% at Fujisawa-Honmachi) and about 45% by 16+ minutes city-wide (121.1万円/坪 within 5 minutes vs 66.3 at 16+); house prices fall only ~19% over the same range. Used houses transacted at about ¥158万/tsubo city-wide (floor-area basis): Kugenuma district ~195, Tsujido ~187, the Fujisawa centre ~165; by age, ≤10-yr stock ~183 falls to ~125 for 30+-yr stock — a shallow gradient, because in the shore districts the land is most of the price. The district prints of ~264 for Kugenuma-Tachibana houses and ~205 for its land blend station-front commercial streets with premium residential ones and are ignored as benchmarks. Official residential land prices rose +5.4% in the 2026 公示地価 survey (+4.8% in 基準地価， after +5.0% in 2025) — 55 of 56 residential points rose, with the coast and hub rising about twice as fast as the northern stations.

benchmarks.note: Land benchmarks: residential ¥/tsubo by station, triangulated from MLIT transaction data via Utinokati (multi-year, standardised) and 2026 official land-price points via Totinokati/tochidai/tochi-d: Hon-Atsugi ~85 (2026 official residential points at a 7–10-minute walk price 86–103 — Asahicho 5-chome ~102–103, Kotobukicho ~91, Asahicho 3-chome ~86; Utinokati's station regression of ~26 and station simple average of ~41 are NOT used — their 'Hon-Atsugi catchment' averages a 69-minute walk, sweeps in the Aikawa/Kiyokawa fringe and urbanisation-control deals, and is a rural number wearing a station's name; the all-use station average of ~86 is likewise not used, since it mixes Nakacho commercial points at ~443–512 in with the residential tail and only coincides with the residential figure), Aiko-Ishida ~55 (official points at 9–10 minutes 57–64 against a compact transaction catchment — regression ~40 at a 16-minute average walk, Aiko district deals ~50). Atsugi City contains exactly two stations, both Odakyu; Atsugi Station itself stands in Ebina, across the Sagami River, and no record in this collection uses it. Urbanisation-control (調整区域) land in Atsugi transacts at ~12万円/坪 across 68 deals against ~45 for urbanised residential land, and the city transaction pool averages 96-tsubo lots, so every wide-catchment average is dragged; control-area listings are major-caution, land-utility cases, never comparables. Walk bands use Atsugi's observed land gradient — official Hon-Atsugi residential points fall ~22% by 11–15 minutes and ~37% by 17–24 minutes, roughly −25% by a 10-minute walk and −40% at 16+ minutes for land; house prices show no such gradient in the data (16+-minute houses ~85 against the ~88 city anchor). Used houses transacted at about ¥88万/tsubo city-wide (floor-area basis, standardised): by age on the station regression curves, near-new stock ~118–129 falls to ~90–99 at 10 years, ~71–77 at 20 and ~61–64 at 30+; the ≤5-minute-walk house print of ~284 is commercial-mixed (it includes a ¥4.5億 shop/house deal) and is ignored, as is Aiko-Higashi's thin ~235 district print. Official residential land prices rose +2.4% in the 2026 公示地価 survey (33 points, none down; commercial +7.3%, and +9.3% in the 2026 基準地価) — a steady, commercial-led rise, the fifth straight annual increase on the Hon-Atsugi series, not a Matsudo-style acceleration.
